## 103. The presentation under a browser: vendor defaults, narrow viewports, the PDF export and a missing runtime

A runtime review drove the delivered presentation in a real browser at four viewport
widths, through its PDF export, and with each of its three remote runtimes blocked in
turn. It returned FAIL on thirty-two findings: no Critical, eight Major, seventeen
Minor and seven informational. None was a defect in application code. Every Major was
a condition no contract test in this suite could have seen, because each is a property
of what a browser computes rather than of what the source says &mdash; a gradient painted
twice at two aspect ratios, text scaled to two pixels, a page count fixed before a
diagram was drawn, and a single failed module fetch taking the whole deck with it. The
rows below own the choices those fixes required. Five findings were confirmed as
needing nothing and are recorded in 103.8 rather than fixed.


### 103.1 The delivered slide count, reconciled against the plan

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.1.1 | **Keep eighteen sections and reconcile the plan's stated target here, rather than merging two slides to reach sixteen** | (a) Merge the release-gate slide into the risk slide and the open-items slide into the closing slide, reaching sixteen; (b) delete one of the two; (c) change the count AAP &sect;0.11.2 names; (d) leave the divergence unrecorded, as it was | The plan states a target of sixteen and a **checkable** bound of twelve to eighteen, and its verification sentence names the bound, not the target &mdash; eighteen satisfies it. The two slides beyond sixteen were not drift: rows 42.8.2 and 84.10.4 each **added** one at an earlier review's direction, row 96.5.2 already rejected merging them, and `test_the_release_gate_slide_stands_on_its_own` now asserts one of them is a slide of its own. So (a) would reverse two accepted decisions and fail a delivered case, and it was rejected once already on the ground that merging risks the checked four-bullet and forty-word caps. (b) discards content two reviews asked for. (c) edits a frozen plan. (d) is the finding: the divergence was real and this log had never owned it | The delivered count sits at the top of the permitted range, so a nineteenth section would breach Rule 2. Two cases bound that from both sides &mdash; `test_the_section_count_is_within_the_fixed_bounds` and `test_the_deck_holds_the_section_count_rule_2_allows` &mdash; and `test_the_presentation_keeps_its_structure` pins the exact figure, so an addition fails three cases rather than passing quietly |
| 103.1.2 | **Correct the two docstrings in `backend/tests/security/test_documentation_contract.py` that still described the deck as sixteen slides** | (a) Leave them, since the constant they sit beside is correct and no case fails; (b) delete the sentences; (c) change `DECK_SLIDES` to sixteen to match the prose | The module's header summary and the structure case's docstring both said *sixteen slides* while `DECK_SLIDES = 18` two hundred lines above asserted eighteen. The prose a reader consults to learn the contract contradicted the contract. (a) leaves a reader to discover which of the two is authoritative. (b) removes an accurate summary line to fix one word in it. (c) would break the delivered deck against its own suite | Prose in a docstring is read by no gate, so it can go stale again. What bounds it is that the figure now appears once as prose beside the constant that enforces it, and the constant is what every assertion reads |


### 103.2 Vendor defaults the deck had not overridden

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.2.1 | **Scope the three gradient rules to `.reveal .slides section.slide-*` and give the six dark sections `data-background-color`**, rather than leaving the selectors unscoped | (a) Keep the unscoped selectors and accept the double paint; (b) drop `!important` alone; (c) hide the framework's generated backdrop layer entirely; (d) set the gradient on the backdrop and not on the section | The framework copies a section's class list onto a generated backdrop element, so `.slide-title { background: <gradient> }` painted **both** boxes &mdash; and it paints them at different sizes. Measured: the section occupied 38.40, 21.60, 1843.20 x 1036.80 while the backdrop occupied 0, 0, 1920 x 1080, an inset of exactly `0.04 x 1920 / 2`, which is the framework's undeclared default margin. The visible seam was the title slide's scrim clipped to the smaller box over an unscrimmed gradient beneath, measured at up to (-52, -51, -77) per channel. So the fix is two-part and neither half suffices: scope the rules off the backdrop **and** declare `margin: 0`. The attribute is then what gives the backdrop a flat navy. (a) is the finding. (b) leaves both boxes painted. (c) would lose the framework's own contrast detection, which reads the backdrop's colour. (d) would break the print export, where the framework deletes the backdrop layer outright | The attribute is markup rather than a stylesheet rule, so a seventh dark section added later would need it too, and nothing fails if it is omitted. What made this detectable in the first place was sampling the border pixels of a rendered frame; after the fix, 0 of 5,998 sampled seam pixels have all three channels above 200, and the section and backdrop rects coincide exactly at 0, 0, 1920 x 1080 |
| 103.2.2 | **Style the navigation chevrons and the progress bar in the inline theme**, rather than relying on the framework's contrast detection alone | (a) Leave the defaults; (b) set only the chevrons; (c) invert the progress bar's own colour token | The framework ships `color: #000` on the controls and a `rgba(0,0,0,.2)` track with a white fill, which is correct on a light deck and wrong on this one: measured 2.7:1 on the five gradient slides, and a progress bar that read inverted on every white slide. The contrast class the framework would have used cannot fire for a gradient painted in CSS, since it reads the backdrop element's own colour &mdash; which is precisely what row 103.2.1's attribute supplies, so the two fixes reinforce each other. (b) leaves the progress bar wrong on twelve slides. (c) does not exist as a token | The theme now states these values, so a framework upgrade that changes its defaults changes nothing here. Measured after: chevrons `rgb(148, 250, 213)` at 0.9 opacity, track `rgba(26, 16, 95, 0.18)` at 6px, fill the accent-bar gradient |
| 103.2.3 | **Add `titleColor`, `clusterBkg` and `clusterBorder` to the diagram theme variables** | (a) Leave them, since the diagrams render; (b) restyle the cluster elements with CSS after each render; (c) drop the subgraph containers from the data-flow diagram | The five variables the plan enumerates do not cover subgraph containers, so both cluster labels rendered black and their borders `rgb(238, 242, 217)` &mdash; a colour from no part of this palette. (a) publishes off-palette chrome on the deck's most-read slide. (b) reaches into a third party's generated markup after the fact and would run again on every re-render. (c) removes the before-and-after structure the slide exists to show | Three variables beyond the plan's five. They are additive and named, and measured after the change the cluster borders are `rgb(91, 57, 243)` on white with `rgb(26, 16, 95)` labels |


### 103.3 Layout and density

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.3.1 | **Give the KPI grid three columns at every desktop width and let the icon row fit its own children** | (a) Leave the five-column base rule; (b) add a fourth breakpoint for each width where the hole appeared; (c) author a ninth and a fourth item so the declared tracks fill | Nine cards in `repeat(5, ...)` leave a hole at 1920, 1440 and 1401, and only the sub-1400 band rendered a clean three-by-three; separately, `.icon-row` declared four tracks and carried three items on two slides, leaving the last card 287.04px short of the container it was meant to align with. (a) is the finding. (b) multiplies breakpoints to state one intention. (c) invents content to satisfy a stylesheet, and the four-bullet cap would refuse it. Three columns divide nine exactly, and `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(180px, 1fr))` lets a three-item row occupy its full width | The auto-fit form re-flows if an item is added, which is the intent. Measured after: `553.328px` three-up at 1920, 1440 and 1401, and the last icon card's right edge flush with the table's at 1229.33 |
| 103.3.2 | **Raise the foot paragraph's selector specificity and separate the four pairs of touching elements**, rather than adjusting the shared element rules | (a) Change `.reveal p` so the foot inherits the spacing it wants; (b) set the spacing inline on each element; (c) leave them touching | `.slide-foot { margin-top: 28px }` is a (0, 1, 0) selector losing to the framework's `.reveal p { margin: 0 0 14px }` at (0, 1, 1), so the declared gap measured 0.00px. Three further pairs measured 0.00px: a table against the heading after it, and the closing slide's foot and sub-line against the accent bar. (a) changes spacing on every paragraph in the deck to fix one class. (b) is the construct Rule 2's theme requirement exists to avoid. (c) is the finding | Four scoped rules where the framework's own element rules would otherwise apply. Each is a single declaration and each was measured after the change: 18.67, 18.66 and 21.34 screen pixels, from 28 and 32 authored |
| 103.3.3 | **Stop the short-viewport rule overriding the vertical centring, and give the release-gate table an untinted baseline row** | (a) Keep the override and accept top-aligned dividers; (b) remove the short-viewport rule entirely; (c) drop the row flags from the gate table | A `max-height` rule intended for dense content slides flipped `justify-content` to `flex-start` on **all eighteen**, leaving 482px of dead space below a divider's content at 1280x800. Separately the gate table flagged rows one and three while even rows were zebra-striped, so no row showed the plain surface a reader calibrates the flags against. (b) would reintroduce the overflow the rule was written for. (c) discards the flags' meaning | The centring is now expressed once, and the deck-wide margin-box asymmetry measures 0.01px at 1280x800. The `no-zebra` class is markup, so a future table wanting the same treatment must opt in |


### 103.4 The narrow-viewport canvas

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.4.1 | **Make the presentation canvas the viewport's own box below 1025px, keeping the authored 1920x1080 canvas above it and for every print export** | (a) Keep the fixed canvas and let the framework scale it down; (b) adopt the framework's alternative scrolling view below a threshold; (c) reduce the minimum scale so more of the deck fits; (d) publish a separate narrow document | The framework scales a fixed canvas to fit, so at 768px the scale measured 0.384 and text landed at 4.42 to 5.41 effective pixels, and at 375px the scale hit the 0.2 minimum exactly and text measured 2.30 to 2.82 pixels &mdash; unreadable, and a clamp means the deck was already as large as that approach can make it. Setting the canvas to the viewport makes the scale exactly 1.0, so an authored pixel is a rendered pixel. (a) is the finding. (b) is row 103.4.2's subject and was measured to break navigation. (c) makes text smaller still. (d) is a second deliverable where Rule 2 requires one self-contained file | The canvas now changes kind on resize, so every diagram must be re-drawn when it does, and the print export must be held to the desktop canvas explicitly. Both are done in the bootstrap and both are asserted by measurement: scale is exactly 1 at 320, 375, 500, 768 and 1024, the minimum effective text rose from 2.30px to **11.52px**, and `test_the_deck_declares_responsive_behaviour` pins the breakpoint literals |
| 103.4.2 | **Declare `scrollActivationWidth: 0`, disabling the framework's alternative scrolling view at every width** | (a) Leave it undeclared at its default of 435px; (b) declare the scrolling view as the deliberate narrow-width mode; (c) raise the threshold above every width the deck is read at | Only five framework options were declared, so this one inherited 435px and the deck silently entered a different view below that width &mdash; where the measured consequences were that the location hash was never rewritten, a deep link was dropped one time in five, `Reveal.slide()` no-opped or landed one slide off, and two sections were marked current at once. (b) would accept all of that. (c) states the same intention less clearly. Activation requires the configured value to be a number at least the presentation width, so zero can never satisfy it | One more declared option, which is what the plan's frozen option set is for &mdash; the five it names are untouched. Verified across 320, 375, 500, 768, 1024, 1025 and 1920: no scroll-view class, zero scroll-view nodes, and **exactly one** section marked current at every width, with the hash tracking correctly to `#/11` |
| 103.4.3 | **Re-emit each diagram top-down below 1025px and draw it at intrinsic size inside a horizontally pannable container when a fitted width would put its labels under 11px** | (a) Always fit the diagram to the container; (b) always draw at intrinsic size; (c) hide the diagrams at narrow widths; (d) author a second, narrower source for each | Fitting a 2490px-wide drawing into a 327px column paints 16px labels at 6.33px. (a) is that outcome. (b) forces a pan even at 768px, where fitting still leaves 13.10px. (c) removes half the deck's two non-text visuals, which Rule 2 requires. (d) is content duplication that would drift. The rewrite is two substitutions on the stowed source, and the branch is chosen from the measured ratio against an 11px floor | The container hands its vertical axis to the slide body, which took three attempts to get right: as a flex item it collapsed to 407px of a 1662px drawing and clipped the rest unreachably, and `flex-shrink: 0` is what fixed it. Verified at 375, 500, 700 and 768: labels at 16.00px on the intrinsic branch, the pan opening at the exact midpoint, and **15 of 15** nodes reachable at every width |
| 103.4.4 | **Signal recoverable content with a two-layer scroll shadow on the slide body and a sticky slide head, rather than a visible scrollbar** | (a) Style the scrollbar with `::-webkit-scrollbar`; (b) set `scrollbar-width` so a gutter is reserved; (c) add a permanent visual cue; (d) leave the truncation unsignalled | Between 436 and 720px five slides were truncated at rest with nothing to say so. The obvious fix does not work here: this browser paints **overlay** scrollbars that reserve zero layout space, measured as `offsetWidth - clientWidth == 0` on all 36 probes, and setting the standard property additionally disables the vendor pseudo-element rules. A background layer attached `local` over one attached `scroll` is deterministic instead &mdash; it appears only while content lies below and vanishes at the end of the scroll. (c) would show a cue on slides that fit. (d) is the finding | The cue is subtle by construction. Measured at 768: a monotonic ramp from 248 to 219 in the gutters at rest, pure white at maximum scroll, and nothing on a slide that fits. The sticky head needed its own `box-shadow: 0 -60px 0 0` cover, because this browser anchors a sticky element to the scroll container's content-box edge and the container's top padding would otherwise show content passing behind the heading; verified as zero non-white pixels across every row above the head |


### 103.5 The PDF export, and motion

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.5.1 | **Change one selector from the child combinator to a descendant combinator, and guard every responsive block with `html:not(.print-pdf)`** | (a) Duplicate the rule for the print case; (b) target the framework's page wrapper directly; (c) accept the export as degraded | The export re-parents every section into a generated page wrapper, so `.reveal .slides > section` stopped matching and the slides lost their height &mdash; measured as 745px of a 1867px slide cut on roughly nine of twelve content pages. Proved load-bearing on the fixed build: on the first page `.reveal .slides section.slide-title` matches and the child form does **not**, and the framework **deletes** the backdrop layer in print, so without this the six dark slides would export white on white. The guard is needed because a narrow export viewport would otherwise apply tablet rules to a 1920px canvas. (a) states one intention twice. (b) couples the theme to a generated class name | The export now depends on a selector shape, which is easy to reintroduce. It is verified by measurement rather than by reading: 0 pixels lost to clipping across 898 descendants, and all six dark pages painting with `print-color-adjust: exact` |
| 103.5.2 | **Stow each diagram's source before the framework starts and hold the print draw until the page wrappers exist, rather than drawing on the ready event** | (a) Draw on ready, as before; (b) clamp an undrawn diagram's height in CSS for the print case; (c) drop the diagrams from the export; (d) draw before initialising | Four attempts failed here and each failure is worth recording. The framework fixes each page's height from the slide's own content **after** ready and re-parents every section afterwards: an instrumented timeline put ready at 106ms with zero page wrappers present, the restored source making one slide 806px taller at 106.7ms, and the wrappers arriving at 212ms. So drawing on ready both inflated the measurement &mdash; one page measured 2158px, two sheets, on **nine of nine** loads &mdash; and left the renderer measuring text in a tree being rebuilt, which corrupted it on **seven of nine** loads. (b) was tried and deadlocked: a zero height made the node fail the bootstrap's own layout gate, so it was never drawn and never released. (d) draws before any slide has a box. Emptying the nodes keeps the source out of the measurement; polling for the wrappers puts the draw after the rebuild | Two mechanisms the export now depends on, one of them a bounded poll. Determinism is the property that matters and it was measured rather than assumed: six loads by four different routes gave **all 18 pages at exactly 1079px** and both diagrams at full size with 15 nodes, and four separate sheets are byte-identical by digest between an early load and the last |
| 103.5.3 | **Widen the diagram failure marker to test the width actually drawn, rather than the renderer's own completion attribute** | (a) Keep the attribute test; (b) inspect the drawing's node count; (c) report every failure from the promise rejection alone | The marker selected only nodes without the completion attribute, which the renderer sets **before** it can fail &mdash; so a corrupted render was silent, and the degenerate export above passed every check the deck could make about itself. A drawn width under 40px is the observable that distinguishes a real drawing from an error placeholder. (a) is the hole. (b) is a weaker signal, since an error placeholder can carry nodes. (c) misses a render that resolves and produces nothing | The threshold is a constant. It never fires on a healthy load, verified across eight cold loads and six exports, and it fires correctly in all four blocked-runtime scenarios. The marker also now logs only when it actually marks something, which held it to 10 records per eighteen-slide walk instead of 18 |
| 103.5.4 | **Extend the reduced-motion rule to the framework's background layers and its progress bar** | (a) Leave the rule on the slide sections; (b) declare a global transition reset | The rule reached the sections but not the generated backdrop, so an 0.8s cross-fade persisted for a reader who had asked for less motion &mdash; the most visible movement in the deck. (b) reaches elements whose transitions are not motion | Two selectors added to an existing block. Measured under real emulation: backgrounds instant across 40 samples with zero intermediate frames and the progress bar instant, against a control showing 43 and 47 distinct intermediate values with emulation off |


### 103.6 A deck that survives its own missing runtimes

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.6.1 | **Move the diagram runtime's import into a module script of its own that publishes it on `window`, rather than converting it to a caught dynamic import** | (a) A caught dynamic `import()` in the bootstrap; (b) leave the static import and add a fallback classic script that re-bootstraps; (c) load the runtime from a second origin | The bootstrap opened with a static `import`, so a blocked fetch aborted the **whole** module: the framework was never initialised, and its stylesheet leaves every non-current slide hidden, so blocking one asset of three produced a completely blank navy page. (a) was the first choice and is arguably cleaner, but `test_the_diagram_module_carries_its_hash_in_the_import_map` pins the literal `import mermaid from 'mermaid';`, and although that case's own comment shows its subject is the **bare specifier** &mdash; which a dynamic import preserves &mdash; a correct fix that needs no test changed is preferable to one that needs a security case rewritten. Splitting the import is that fix: the literal survives byte-for-byte, and a module script whose fetch fails aborts only its own graph while later in-order module scripts still run. (b) duplicates the bootstrap. (c) adds an origin the content policy would have to name | A second module script, and a bootstrap that reads a global rather than an import binding. Verified with the runtime 404'd: the deck presents, all eighteen slides render, all forty-seven icons draw, and both diagrams degrade to a legible notice at 9.3:1 |
| 103.6.2 | **Substitute a marking-only stand-in for each missing runtime, rather than guarding every call site** | (a) Test for the runtime at each of the four call sites; (b) let the calls throw and catch at the top level; (c) report the absence and draw nothing | The deck's three diagnostic branches and both failure markers were unreachable code, because the module that held them never ran when anything upstream failed. A stand-in that rejects every draw makes the existing failure path do the work, and matches the shape the icon guard already used. (a) would put four tests where one substitution serves, and `test_the_render_cycle_is_wired_to_both_events` fixes the number of draw calls at exactly two, so extra guarded call sites are not available. (b) leaves the deck in whatever state the throw interrupted. (c) is what the stand-in produces, by the route the deck already has | Two stand-ins that must keep the shape of the runtimes they replace. Each was driven to fire: with the icon runtime blocked, all 47 placeholders are marked and the guard logs once; with the framework blocked, the exact 61-character message is logged once, compared codepoint by codepoint |
| 103.6.3 | **Hide speaker notes and undrawn diagram source from the inline theme, and stow the sources whether or not the framework loads** | (a) Rely on the vendor stylesheet, as before; (b) remove the notes from the document; (c) hide the notes only, leaving the diagram sources to the stow alone | The vendor stylesheet was the **only** thing hiding eleven blocks of internal reviewer prose, and both diagram nodes held their raw source as text &mdash; so losing that one asset published both. The stow ran inside the branch that requires the framework, which is exactly the case where it is needed most. (b) discards content the presenter uses. (c) leaves a window in which restored source can paint | Two theme rules and a moved call. Verified under a full blackout with the vendor sheet contributing zero rules: eleven notes hidden with zero visible text nodes originating in them, twenty-four of twenty-six authored diagram constructs absent from the document entirely, and &mdash; measured across the whole 1920x11099 page &mdash; every glyph-edge pixel but 0.0023% accounted for by a visible authored text node, with zero hot tiles of 36,960 |
| 103.6.4 | **Give an unfilled icon slot a dashed square, in the accent colour on the six slides that paint a dark ground, selected through the authored slide classes** | (a) One border colour everywhere; (b) select the dark case through the framework's own dark-background class; (c) leave an unavailable icon invisible; (d) substitute a text glyph | A marked placeholder had no visual treatment at all, so a missing icon read as nothing. One colour is not enough: the palette's deepest violet measured **1.06:1** against the hero gradient and **1.02:1** against a divider, visible by hue alone. (b) is the obvious selector and is wrong for the case that matters &mdash; under a blackout the framework never runs and applies no classes, so the treatment would vanish precisely when every icon is missing. The authored classes are in the markup and always present. (c) is the finding. (d) puts a character where an icon belongs | Two rules and a colour split that must stay aligned with which slides are dark. Measured on both failure paths: 7.10, 7.64 and 13.17:1 on the dark slides and 9.33 and 8.23:1 on the light ones, and under blackout **six of six** dark markers and **forty-one of forty-one** light markers correct |


### 103.7 The response header, and a row this round withdraws

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.7.1 | **Remove `ambient-light-sensor=()` from the `Permissions-Policy` header, keeping the other thirteen tokens.** This **supersedes row 12.9**, which recorded the token as deliberately retained | (a) Keep it, as row 12.9 decided; (b) remove the header; (c) keep the token and suppress the warning in the viewer | Row 12.9 declined to act because the finding was informational and every change had to trace to a named finding. It now traces to one: this round's review raised it as G1 and reproduced it at runtime, so the condition the earlier row rested on no longer holds. The token names a feature no browser implements, so it denies nothing and reports itself on every HTML page load from this origin. Removing it makes the header state only denials that take effect. (b) would remove thirteen denials that do work. (c) is not available for a response header | Thirteen tokens rather than fourteen. If a browser ever implements the feature, the header no longer denies it &mdash; and the header would then be one token short of the posture it had, which is why the removal is recorded here rather than made silently. No test pins the token or the count |


### 103.8 Findings this round confirmed as needing nothing

Five of the thirty-two were verified against the running system rather than assumed,
and each turned out to need no change. They are recorded because a finding closed
without a reason reads later as a finding missed.

| # | Decision | Alternatives considered | Rationale | Risks |
|---|----------|------------------------|-----------|-------|
| 103.8.1 | **Leave the presentation's layout transform alone.** A malformed transform was reported on cold load and did not reproduce | (a) Write an explicit transform on every load; (b) add a defensive reset | Not reproduced in eight further cold loads, over 21,912 computed-transform reads including pseudo-elements, following nine earlier clean loads. The container computes `none`, which is **correct** at a scale of exactly 1: the framework passes an empty layout transform when the scale is 1, confirmed by the inline property being the empty string and by a 1025px viewport producing a well-formed matrix instead. The report most likely read `none` as absent | A condition that cannot be reproduced cannot be regression-tested. What bounds it is that the transform is now measured on every runtime sweep |
| 103.8.2 | **Leave the two blocked source-map fetches as they are** | (a) Name the delivery network in a `connect-src` allowance; (b) drop the integrity attributes so no map is sought | Both blocked URLs are debugger sidecars the document never references, and the developer-tools issue payload carries an **empty** source location where a page-caused violation would name a script and a line. Page-originated console messages measure **zero**, and instrumentation installed before any page script proved the document issues no request of its own. (a) would widen the policy to admit traffic only a debugger makes. (b) removes an integrity guarantee to quiet a tool | The entries appear whenever a reader has developer tools open. They are inert, and the policy that produces them is the one Rule 2 requires |
| 103.8.3 | **Take no action on two sections being marked current at once**, which row 103.4.2 makes unreachable | (a) Add a corrective pass after each navigation; (b) assert the invariant at runtime | The condition existed only inside the framework's alternative scrolling view, and declaring `scrollActivationWidth: 0` means activation can never be satisfied. Verified across seven widths from 320 to 1920px: exactly one section marked current in every case, before and after navigating | The condition returns if that option is ever removed. It is one of the two options row 103.4.2 adds, and both are asserted by the responsive-behaviour case |
| 103.8.4 | **Leave the documentation viewer's enforced policy as it is** | (a) Admit the viewer's source maps; (b) relax the policy on those two pages | One blocked source-map fetch per documentation page, from the same cause as row 103.8.2 and with the same absence of effect. The policy is what makes each inline script admitted by its own digest, which a delivered case asserts | Unchanged from row 103.8.2: visible to a reader with developer tools open, inert otherwise |
| 103.8.5 | **Report the browser client's build failure rather than fixing it** | (a) Add the missing package and correct the eighteen type errors; (b) remove the module that fails; (c) exclude it from the build | Its source is reference-only under AAP &sect;0.6.1.7 and out of scope under &sect;0.9.2, which directs that a finding outside the boundary be reported. The failure is a missing payment package and eighteen type errors in one module, all predating this work, and it is already recorded as an open item. (a) edits read-only source. (b) and (c) change delivered behaviour to make a build pass | The client remains unbuildable, which the delivered architecture diagram states on its face by drawing it as unconnected, and which the open-item registers carry. `test_the_deck_reports_the_open_items_explicitly` keeps that disclosure present |
